comments.author: @tysoncung
comments.text: The part I still find hard to believe: the 1998 Brasilia act put the border exactly where Peru had always said it should be, and Ecuador's compensation was one square kilometre at Tiwinza held as private property under Ecuadorian law, on Peruvian sovereign soil. Ownership without sovereignty. Ecuador also took navigation rights on the Amazon and trade centres inside Peru. Sources are listed in the description. If you were negotiating for Ecuador, would you have taken the square kilometre or the river access?
